subject: Post-demo: Apex Analytics benchmark plan & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@apexanalytics.com>
Cc: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@apexanalytics.com>, dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Apex Analytics benchmark plan & next steps

Hi Olivia / Daniel,

Thanks again for the time this morning — really helpful to understand the ingest profile and the latency SLAs you
need for the insights UI. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight benchmark so we can validate cost/latency tradeoffs vs
the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Summary of needs (from call):
- Serving surface: near-realtime single-turn generation for autosummaries + multi-turn chat for analyst workflows
- P95 latency target (UI): <= 300ms for 512-token requests (peak interactive path)
- Burst throughput: 300-500 concurrent requests during morning ingest window
- Budget sensitivity: looking to reduce per-token cost vs current hyperscaler baseline by ~20-30%

Proposed next step: 48-hour A/B benchmark comparing Redwood hosted runtime vs Apex’s current hyperscaler API (they use Vertex + custom autoscaling). Plan attached (redwood-benchmark-plan.pdf) but high level:
1) Two identical request traces (prod-sampled): small-chat (avg 120 tokens) and long-summary (avg 512 tokens)
2) Run concurrent load profiles at 1x, 2x, and 4x baseline concurrency to observe tokens/sec and p95/p99
3) Collect: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, error-rate, and cost-per-1k-tokens for each run
4) Validate model parity: output-quality checks using your sample prompt set (we’ll run a blind shuffle eval)

Deliverables:
- Raw metrics + cost model (spreadsheet)
- Short write-up on tradeoffs and recommended config (batching, KV caching enabled, suggested quantization)
- Short demo of routing/fallback policy if needed (can show automatic fallback to lower-cost variant under heavy load)

Can we schedule the benchmark to start Friday 7/17 (your morning)? If so, please confirm the test traces (I attached apx-sample-traces.txt) and whether we should hit your staging endpoints or you want Redwood to exercise live prod traffic in read-only mode.

Thanks — I’ll loop Dev on the technical plan once you confirm timing.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Ben — thanks for the note and outline. This looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications before we lock Friday: 

- For the 512-token path — that’s for the autosummary endpoint only, correct? Our analyst chat can often be 200–700 tokens depending on the chain.
- On model parity: we need to be careful around hallucination risk for the summary path. Can you confirm which model versions you plan to test vs our baseline (they use Vertex with gpt-3.5-like open weights)?
- Staging vs prod: prefer staging for the first run. We’ll provide a staging endpoint and short-lived API key.

I’ll confirm with Procurement about the test window (they pushed some vendor approvals today). Assuming they sign off, Friday morning Pacific works on our side.

Olivia
Sr. Product Manager — Insights
Apex Analytics
olivia.park@apexanalytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@apexanalytics.com>, Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@apexanalytics.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-07-14T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Apex Analytics benchmark plan & next steps

Thanks — quick answers inline and a couple of small asks.

- 512-token path: correct — that’s the autosummary endpoint profile. For analyst chat we’ll include an expanded "long-chat" trace that has a 200–700 token distribution; we’ll provide both so you can map which route is dominant in production.
- Models: we’ll test the following variants:
  * Redwood-verified-7b-fp16 (baseline low-latency)
  * Redwood-7b-8bit (quantized profile)
  * Redwood-13b-16bit (higher-quality baseline)
  * Hyperscaler-equivalent (open checkpoint that matches their gpt-3.5-like baseline)

We won’t compare proprietary closed models directly against your Vertex paid model — instead we’ll benchmark the open-equivalent they’ve been using so the comparison is apples-to-apples on model family and compute type. If you want us to run a paid-hyperscaler run we can but that requires billing approvals.

Staging endpoint works. For the metric collection: can you provide a staging API key scoped to rate-limit to 600 rps? That will let us safely ramp to 4x concurrency without affecting other services.

Attaching the full test-config (apex-test-config.yml) — shows the exact payload shape, seed prompts, and the A/B split we’ll use. High-level notes from Dev (copied below):

> On Tue, Jul 14, 2026 at 14:05, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> 
> For the p95/p99 targets you mentioned: under Redwood’s continuous batching path we expect to see material improvements for the 120-token path (tokens/sec increases 25–40% vs isolated requests) and tail latency p99 reductions of ~15–25% vs naive HTTP-only setups. For the 512-token path the benefits depend on batching window and KV cache warmup; if we enable prefix caching across repeat prompts expect p95 to drop by ~60–80ms on average.
> 
> Ideal instance profile for the run: one 80GB-A100-equivalent for each test runner group, with 2–3 workers per runner. That maps to tokens/sec of roughly 9–12k tokens/sec sustained on the 7b-8bit config for the small-chat trace (this will vary by request shape).

Next actions for Friday start:
- Olivia: confirm staging API key and rate-limit (600 rps) + confirm procurement sign-off
- Daniel: confirm test traces (I’ll upload the two trace files to the staging bucket once key provided)
- Dev/Marissa: we’ll spin up the Redwood runners and drop the result sheet into the shared HubSpot deal (link in metadata).

If Friday slips, we can do Monday 7/20 — let me know.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Apex Analytics benchmark plan & next steps

Hey all — quick technical addendum before the run. A couple points to watch during A/B: 

1) p95 vs p99: p95 will often reflect batching and cache benefits; p99 will surface tail anomalies like instance preemption or cold KV cache misses. Please capture both separately per-run.

2) Tokens/sec and cost math: we’ll report sustained tokens/sec and per-runized cost-per-1k-tokens. For the quantized 7b-8bit config expect ~30% lower cost than 16-bit on identical throughput. Secondary savings come from prefix caching (we’ll show delta with caching on/off).

3) Error modes: we’ll log rejections (429), timeouts, and malformed outputs — include these in the pivot table so you can see if we trade lower cost for higher error-rate under stress.

4) Model-output parity: we’ll supply a blind evaluation sample and run a 3rd-party scoring script you can run locally if you prefer. That script will compare generation overlap, hallucination cues (entity hallucination score), and factuality heuristics.

5) Runbook (if something spikes): our runner has an automatic fallback to a slightly cheaper variant if latency or error-rate crosses thresholds. We’ll show that behavior in the final demo.

I'll be online Friday morning to stand up the runners and help tune batch windows.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
